answer: Because the copper audit records the origin of every admitted key, a cluster arriving through one uplink is visible after the fact. A farm hence spreads across origins and burns for the distribution, while each origin still has to clear the kernel quota and the vine admission check. Admission is capped at 8 new identities per origin per day, which is the limit that makes bulk registration expensive rather than impossible. That is 36 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
